metadata.description: Permanently delete a DeepSeek Harness session from its sidebar menu, including the conversation files and cached data stored on your PC.
metadata.name: dsh-session-remover

paragraphs.text: Permanently delete a DeepSeek Harness session from its sidebar menu, including the conversation file
s and cached data stored on your PC.
# dsh-session-remover
**Delete a DeepSeek Harness session for good, straight from its `⋯` menu.** One red row, one confirm
ation, and the conversation is gone from DSH *and* from the disk: its JSONL log, its projection cach
e and its place in the workspace registry.
No settings page, no archive manager, no agent tools. English-only interface. Nothing else is added.
**Español** → README.es.md
*The session `⋯` menu: **Delete session** sits in red after the shipped rows (pin, rename, fork, arc
hive, copy Session ID). Workspace and session names are blurred.*
*The confirmation: the session to delete is named in the dialog (blurred here), **Cancel** has the i
nitial focus, and nothing is sent to the Host until you confirm.*
## What it does
- Adds **Delete session** to the `⋯` menu of every session row, in red, ordered after the shipped ro

ws.
- Opens a DSH-styled confirmation that names the exact session; **Cancel** takes the initial foc

us and **Escape** closes the dialog without doing anything.
- Closes the session before touching sto
rage. If it is open, the plugin runs the same ordered teardown DSH uses for its own agents (stop, dr

ain, release the writer, detach) and waits for it to finish.
- Removes the session's own directory `

<session store>/<project>/<session-id>/`, including its `.v4.jsonl.zstd` log.
- Removes the derived
cache record `storages/session_projcache/sessions/<session-id>.json`, so no cached title or message

text survives.
- Cleans the workspace registry: detaches the session from every workspace that lists

it, unpins it and clears its archive marker.
- Refreshes the sidebar, and clears the main panel if
the deleted session was the one on screen.
## What it does not do
- **Does not delete attachments.** Images and files live in a content-addressed shared store (`attac
hments/v1/objects/<hash>`) that other sessions may reference, so they are left alone. See What stays

on disk.
- Does not touch other sessions, the files of your workspace, DSH logs, backups or any clo

ud copy.
- Does not add a settings page, an archive browser or a history search.
- Does not add an a

gent tool or a slash command: deletion is user-only and confirmed in the UI.
- Does not make any net

a slash command: deletion is user-only and confirmed in the UI.
- Does not make any network request.
## Why there are no settings
The only decision is which session to delete, and that is already an argument of the action. There i
s no threshold to tune, no interval, no key, no scope. A config page would be a second place to expl
ain the same single behaviour.
## Requirements

- **DSH Desktop** `>= 0.2.1-rc.3`, profile `desktop` (tested on `0.2.1-rc.3`, Windows 11).
- The def

ault per-session **JSONL** session store. A non-JSONL backend is refused at load time.
- Node 22+ (D

SH ships its own runtime).
- **One restart after installing or updating the plugin.** The Host half
intercepts the agent lifecycle, so it can only close sessions that were opened *after* it loaded. Se
ssions opened before that are refused, not half-deleted.
## What gets deleted
| Path | What it is |
| `<session store>/<project>/<session-id>/` | The session's own directory: its versioned `.jsonl.zst

d` log and anything beside it |
| `storages/session_projcache/sessions/<session-id>.json` | Cached p

rojections: title, message-derived values |
| `storages/workspace.json` | Only the references: the s
ession is detached, unpinned and unarchived |
Nothing else is removed. The session is not moved to a recycle bin: the files are deleted, so the sp
ace is returned immediately.
## What stays on disk
**Attachments.** Images and files are stored once per content hash under `attachments/v1/objects/`.
A forked session inherits references to the same hashes, so deleting the objects would break the for
k's images. DSH keeps no reference count, so the plugin leaves them alone rather than guessing.
For a text-only conversation this is nothing at all. If your goal is reclaiming disk space, images a
re what dominates — that cleanup needs a scan of the remaining logs and is deliberately out of scope
ominates — that cleanup needs a scan of the remaining logs and is deliberately out of scope for now.
Also untouched: DSH's own logs, your workspace files, backups you made yourself and any copy that al
ready left the machine.
## How it works
The **Host** half registers one route, `POST /plugins/session-remover/delete`:
1. The request must pass the Host's own request fence and carry the `x-session-remover-confirmation:

delete-session` header. A link, an HTML form or a cross-site request cannot produce that header.
2.

The session id is validated (`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,127}$`) before it can name a path.
3. A l
ive agent is closed through the `AgentHandle` that `ctx.agents.create`/`resume` returned. DSH expose
s no dispose on the registry itself, so the plugin keeps those handles as they are created and refus

es to delete when it has none.
4. The storage directory is resolved from `sessionPersistence.stat` +
`locate` and cross-checked by scanning the store root, then required to be exactly `<root>/<one pro

ject segment>/<session id>`, a real directory, containing a session log file.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility

| DSH | `>= 0.2.1-rc.3` (tested on `0.2.1-rc.3`) |
| Node | `>= 22` |
| OS | Windows 11 (tested); ma

cOS and Linux untested |
| Profile | `desktop` (tested); `web` untested |
| Session store | per-sess

ion JSONL backend (the default) |
| Catalog | listed on dsh-plugin.org |
Validation status: **tested on Windows 11 with DSH Desktop 0.2.1-rc.3** (2026-10-26). The menu row a
nd the confirmation were used through the interface; a real session (a fork) was deleted and its dir
ectory, its projection-cache record and its workspace references were verified gone afterwards, with
a sibling session left intact.
Not validated: macOS, Linux, the web profile and other DSH versions.
## Privacy

- No network access, no telemetry, no external service.
- No cookies, no tokens, no credentials read

.
- The confirmation dialog sends only the session id.
- The interface text is English only, by desi

gn.
- The screenshots above come from a real session; workspace and session names are blurred.
